_comment: Every path in this repo belongs to exactly one class.
TOOL    = code, docs, and reference material ABOUT the tool. Public.
FIXTURE = LIFELIKE test data, whose real counterpart sits in the operator's
life and is structurally indistinguishable. Must be regenerable.
DATA    = anything a REAL RUN produced and the tool reads back. Never tracked;
lives in a private companion store, with a schema shipped here.
Enforced by guards/tools/data_boundary.py in .githooks and in CI.
_audited:
2026-09-21. The question is whether shipped code can put real-run output at a repo-relative path, and whether anything here is lifelike data. Both lists come out empty, and both are conclusions rather than defaults.

DATA: this library drives a remote machine and can capture its screen. VmSession.screenshot() writes wherever the caller says, and both examples pass a bare filename, which resolves to the working directory -- the repo root when run as documented. Such a file shows whatever was on that machine. But it is not DATA in the sense this manifest means: nothing reads it back, no run resolves it, and there is no schema to publish, so declaring it would demand a *.jpg.example that could only be a lie. It is incidental output that must simply never be committed, which is what .gitignore says and what the guard's own RUN-SHAPE check enforces independently of this file. secrets.write_env_file writes only to the REMOTE machine and has no local path at all. Nothing else here writes anything.

FIXTURE: the test data is a CDP target list and a few env values -- example.invalid hosts, a token literally spelled 'x', a credential spelled 's3cret'. None of it is lifelike, none has a real counterpart anyone could be tempted to paste in place of it, and a generator for it would guard against nothing.
_armed: Tested, and the first version of this note was WRONG. It claimed data_boundary's RUN-SHAPE check would refuse a force-added screenshot whether or not this manifest mentioned one. It does not: `git add -f screen.jpg` followed by the guard reported 'clean, 22 tracked files carry no real-run shape'. Its heuristic knows jsonl ledgers, dated files under output directories and databases; a bare .jpg is not a shape it recognises, and a screenshot is the only real-run output this repo can produce. That left .gitignore as the whole control, and .gitignore is advisory. The control is now tests/test_repo_hygiene.py, which fails if any image is tracked and also fails if git lists almost nothing -- so it cannot pass by having examined an empty list.
